newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico peso ends firm after expected FOMC decision.
newsitem.headline: Mexico peso ends firm after expected FOMC decision.

text.p: The Mexican peso closed mostly firmer on Tuesday after the outcome of the U.S. Federal Open Market Committee meeting was in line with expectations, traders said.
"Some local corporations and foreign brokers stepped in to sell dollars, but the session was mostly quiet awaiting the result of the FOMC meeting," a trader said.
The benchmark 48-hour peso closed 0.3 of a centavo softer at 7.8930/7.8950 per dollar, while its 24-hour stablemate closed 1.2 centavos firmer at 7.8730/7.8780 per dollar.
"The market had discounted the rates hike for some time, so things stayed calm after the announcement," the trader added.
Minutes before the close of foreign exchange trade in Mexico, the FOMC announced it had raised the federal funds rate by 25 basis points to 5.50 percent.
Same-day peso contracts closed earlier 2.1 centavos firmer at 7.8700/7.8710 per dollar.
Dealers said the 48-hour peso weakened slightly amid demand for dollars in theat market due to the fact that contracts do not require settlement until next Monday.
The advantage, they said, is that dollars bought at 48 hours may be paid for using pesos that can meanwhile be invested in the local money market.
Mexican financial markets will be closed on Thursday and Friday, March 27 and 28, for Easter holiday celebrations.

Traders said that after the market had absorbed the FOMC rate hike decision, the peso could come under slight pressure from month-end corporate demand for dollars and for demand from travelers ahead of the forthcoming long weekend.
"The peso will trade at the same levels as today's as long as some big player does not go long on dollars," a dealer said.
